title: O Lord! Through Thee We Own
description: O Lord! Through Thee We Own in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 246, “Born Again”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord! through Thee we own A new and heav-enly birth, Kin-dred to spi-rits round Thy throne, Though so-journ-ers of earth.

lines: O Lord! through Thee we own
Kindred to spirits round Thy throne,
The life which Thou hast given,
The grave is but the path to heaven,
And death is now our friend.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch died in 1870.
credits: Words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
